messages.text: PR#6 has comments from the human expert reviewer, plesae address them (also fix the merge conflict in the tracking.json)
I’ll read the expert comments on PR #6, address them, and resolve the `tracking.json` conflict while preserving both sets of records. Then I’ll run the relevant checks and push the update.

The expert’s outer-vessel formula uses an undefined “RCM”: RVo = RCMo + 1.75 × (RCM − RVi). May I interpret RCM as the cold-mass inner radius RCMi? I can implement and clearly label that interpretation for the expert’s confirmation.
- Use RCMi provisionally (recommended)
- Wait for expert clarification

The new expert comments specify cold-mass and vessel scaling, energy-based sizing, and a hard 5 T central-field limit. I’ll make those rules enforceable and calculate stored energy for the finite winding model. Full sizing of the iron and toroid configurations will remain conditional on their complete field solutions.

The tracking conflict is resolved by retaining both the magnet and software records. For the sizing study, I’ll provisionally read the undefined `RCM` in the outer-vessel formula as `RCMi` and flag that for expert confirmation. The existing axial allowances were planning choices; I’ll document them explicitly and keep them provisional.

The new sizing rules change the outer-solenoid layout substantially: its provisional vessel outer radius grows from 4.80 m to about 5.40 m. I’m propagating that increase through MAG-03/04’s muon reservations, preserving their allocated depths and gaps. The energy calculation passes refinement and an independent long-solenoid limit check.

All five updated layouts pass the overlap and containment checks, and all 26 magnetic tests pass. The response now separates implemented constraints from open engineering questions: the inner winding’s pack-average current density rises to about 49.6 A/mm², and complete iron/toroid energy calculations are still needed. I’m finishing provenance, review records and CI enforcement before pushing.

The substantive update is pushed, and GitHub reports PR #6 as mergeable. Hosted CI passed, including the new magnetic tests. I’ve posted the detailed response and requested re-review from `mgtmentink`; the `RCM` interpretation and axial allowances remain explicitly open for confirmation.

Updated and pushed [PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6) at `a263a63`.

- Added energy-based sizing, vessel constraints, the 5 T cap, updated layouts and persistent validation rules.
- Resolved `tracking.json`, preserving both contributions.
- Posted the expert response and requested re-review from `mgtmentink`.

Local tests, logging validation and hosted CI pass. PR is mergeable.

`RCM = RCMi`, axial allowances and complete-system field/engineering checks remain explicitly pending confirmation.
